facts.claim: PagerDuty's hosted MCP server is https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp (EU: https://mcp.eu.pagerduty.com/mcp); the self-hosted server is deprecated and its repository archived.
facts.evidence: Support page gives both URLs (updated 2026-09-04); the protected-resource document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp names resource https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp.

facts.claim: PagerDuty does not support dynamic client registration; OAuth needs static client credentials.
facts.evidence: 'PagerDuty does not currently support Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)'; the authorization-server document has no registration_endpoint.

facts.claim: Issuer https://mcp.pagerduty.com/, authorize and token endpoints on app.pagerduty.com/global/oauth; PKCE S256 supported; client_secret_post or basic.
facts.evidence: Discovery document fields; lotrlib.oauth.discover (GET only) resolved hosts [app.pagerduty.com, mcp.pagerduty.com].

facts.claim: Supported scopes include the broad read and write plus per-object scopes (incidents.read, services.write ...); offline_access is not among them.
facts.evidence: scopes_supported (82 entries) includes read and write and not offline_access; the authorization-server document lists the same set.

facts.claim: Tools: browse_* (incidents, services, schedules, teams, event orchestrations, alert grouping, status pages, escalation policies, users, change events, activity) read; manage_* write; manage_teams and manage_alert_grouping include delete; manage_status_pages creates posts; manage_incidents creates and updates incidents.
facts.evidence: Tool table: manage_teams (create, update, delete, add_member, remove_member); manage_alert_grouping (create, update, delete).

facts.claim: The API-key header is 'Authorization: Token token=<key>' (expressible in lotr's mcp-http kind as auth_scheme prefix with auth_prefix 'Token token='); a bearer token (for example a client-credentials app token) is also accepted.
facts.evidence: Authentication section of the integration guide.

facts.claim: The vendor's Claude Code example registers a static localhost redirect, http://localhost:8080/callback; Scoped OAuth apps can be created only by account admins.
facts.evidence: Example uses http://localhost:8080/callback as a static-port illustration.

facts.claim: Requires a PagerDuty account with Advanced Permissions.

choices.because: Hosted official MCP, OAuth discovery published, no DCR; the API-key header format is not expressible by mcp-http.
Narrowest useful scope; offline_access is not offered.
The vendor's example registers a localhost redirect.

choices.decision: consent on manage_incidents, manage_teams, manage_alert_grouping, manage_status_pages
choices.because: They page people, delete, or publish; the rest of manage_* are writes and browse_* reads.

open: Whether PagerDuty accepts the plain-http localhost redirect for a Scoped OAuth app was read only in an example; not tested.
Whether the token endpoint issues a refresh token without offline_access was not checked.
EU authorization-server hosts were not researched.
Tool names come from the integration guide only; not checked against tools/list.
